items.q: What comfort did Cho walk away from, and why?
items.a: Oracle: 100k-person family, ~$1B cash profit a month, four-hour days after 5–6 years. Felt like a **tax office**. Innovation was **bought in**. Approaching 30, vesting options vs Silicon Valley company: **now or never**. He wanted pride that lasts, not rent.

items.q: What rule got him through idea-drop depression?
items.a: **One step per day.** A founder who had made it: I've been there. You do not owe ten steps. Cafe at 9am, nobody looking, thankful for spam. He says he has run that rule for 7–8 years.

items.q: How did Chartmetric get the first dollar?
items.a: Seed empty at 18 months. Self-funded from his account. Charged ~100 betas **$65 / $95** while unready. Same morning: **Rene McLean / RPM paid $950 for a year**. Cho called to refund. McLean: cash is precious at the start, and he would use it 12 months anyway.

items.q: What is Coke-not-Cherry-Coke, and the price yardstick?
items.a: Don't invent a flavor. Persist on the **same job** until duration makes you different (half-price → later premium; Next Big Sound pointed at them). Price ≈ **1/10 of avoided cost** ($140 seat should save $1,400). Independents $20. Ten years is the floor. Aim: Bloomberg for music.
